title: Clivia miniata aurea and Sedum palmeri
Explosion of color
description: I like how all the various flowering plants play off each other, with opposite proportions of the same colors, of equal or more subtle hues.  I don't think this is even a conscious design decision on my part, but simply a matter of "knowing" that these plants seem harmonious together.  The conscious part of the plant selection had more to do with selecting long blooming plants with potential winter into summer bloom for a sunny and occasionally windy location 3 flloors up in the air.  I wanted the color to really pop against the stark white walls of the raised built-in planters, and also contrast against the deep greens of the Quercus agrifolia woodlands beyond.  The textural fuzziness of the Kangaroo Paws also plays off the fuzzy new foliage of the Fern Leaved Banksia.

title: New Guinea Impatiens and Staghorn fern
April flowers in blue vase
description: Collected from the garden for an open house, some of my favorite Asteraceae and Proteaceae as well as Lamiaceae plants. And all of them from south of the border of south of the Equator.

title: Neoregelias colored up in pot
description: Rear garden at 28 Vallejo St, Berkeley, California, container at jacuzzi seat wall.  Some of the dwarfer growing Neoregelia hybrids are quite successful as small container plants in full sun locations here in the San Francisco Bay Area.  This container does not receive any automatic irrigation or misting, but is hand watered about twice a week in summer to retain water in the cup.  The location certainly agrees with these Neo's, as they have taken on some brilliant coloration, and stayed nice and compact in foliage.
